skill.name: quality-gates
skill.description: Run structured quality gates for JavaScript and TypeScript projects, including linting, type checks, tests, builds, audits, and commit checks.
skill.summary: Coordinate staged quality checks before commits, pushes, and deployments.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Static shell, environment, filesystem, and network findings in SKILL.md are documentation false positives caused by Markdown code spans and examples. A medium contextual risk remains because the skill is auto-invoked and recommends package-manager or cleanup commands that can modify a repository.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running lint fixes, audit fixes, package installation, or cleanup commands.

remediation.issue: Package scripts and npx commands can execute project-controlled code.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact command and explain why it is needed before execution, especially in untrusted repositories.
Check that target paths are generated artifacts and ask before deleting them.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Invoked Mutable Command Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill sets auto_invoke to true and recommends commands that can execute project scripts or modify the working tree, including lint fixes, audit fixes, package installs, and build cleanup. This is legitimate quality-gate behavior, but it should require user confirmation before running mutating or package-manager commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show auto invocation plus documented commands that can change files or install dependencies. The intent is quality automation, so the issue is a contextual permission and safety risk rather than malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable checks before code is committed, pushed, or deployed. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through linting, type checks, tests, builds, audits, and commit checks.
actual_capabilities: Detects common JavaScript and TypeScript quality tools from project files and package scripts.
Runs or suggests linting, type checking, unit tests, build verification, and dependency audits.
Defines progressive gate levels for pre-commit, pre-push, and pre-deploy workflows.
Summarizes pass, fail, skipped, duration, error, and coverage details in a clear report.
Checks staged Git changes for common secret names, environment files, and oversized files.
Recommends Husky and lint-staged setup when a project lacks local commit hooks.
limitations: Best suited for Node.js, JavaScript, and TypeScript repositories with standard package scripts.
Command results depend on the local project setup, installed dependencies, and available tools.
Auto-fix commands can change files and should be reviewed before committing.
The skill provides workflow guidance, not a replacement for full CI security policy enforcement.

use_cases.title: Pre-Commit Validation
use_cases.description: Run fast linting and type checks before creating a local commit.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Review
use_cases.description: Run tests, build verification, and dependency audits before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Repository Quality Setup
use_cases.description: Define standard quality gates and recommend commit hook tooling for a project.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the essential quality gates for this project. Start with linting and type checking, then summarize any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and run the pre-commit quality gates. Check for lint errors, type errors, secrets, environment files, and large files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare For Push
prompt_templates.scenario: Broader validation before opening a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the standard pre-push gates for this repository. Include tests, security audit results, and a concise action list for any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Run comprehensive release quality gates. Include build verification, dependency audit status, coverage results, skipped gates, risks, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Run quality gates before I commit this feature.
output_examples.output: The report lists linting and type checking as passed, tests as failed, and build as skipped. It names the failing test suite and gives the next command to reproduce it.

output_examples.input: Check whether this project is ready to deploy.
output_examples.output: The response separates pre-deploy gates by status. It highlights a high dependency vulnerability and recommends fixing it before deployment.

output_examples.input: Set up a quality gate process for this repository.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends essential, standard, and comprehensive gate levels. It also suggests package scripts and a pre-commit hook workflow.

best_practices: Run the fastest gates first so developers get useful feedback quickly.
Review any auto-fix or audit-fix changes before committing them.
Keep project quality thresholds explicit in package scripts or repository configuration.
anti_patterns: Running destructive cleanup commands without checking the target directories first.
Treating warnings, skipped gates, or missing scripts as proof that the project passed.
Using force audit fixes without understanding dependency changes and compatibility risks.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to guide command execution for quality checks. Users should review commands that install, modify, or delete files.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use npm, pnpm, ESLint, Biome, Vitest, Jest, TypeScript, or common build tools.

faq.question: Can it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest auto-fix commands for linting, formatting, and dependency audits. File changes still need human review.

faq.question: Does it replace continuous integration?
faq.answer: No. It helps developers run local gates and prepare for CI, but CI should remain the source of release enforcement.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets?
faq.answer: It checks staged diffs for common secret names and environment file names. Dedicated secret scanning tools provide stronger coverage.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
